## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

```

## Integration with CMake

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
add_executable(${_TEST_NAME}_tests 
    ${_TEST_NAME}_tests.cpp
    test_existing_feature.cpp

```

### Advanced Test Discovery
```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
    TEST_SUFFIX " (auto)"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    EXTRA_ARGS --order rand --warn NoAssertions

endif()

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp

// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

Kenneth, 2026-10-21, on the calibration page I drew: "It looks like you didn't follow this hygiene. read design
guidelines in readme, and fix your own sloppiness", then "I suspect there were more sloppiness in the boards you
designed". He was right on both counts. I had copied markup from older canvas boards (the printer-menu board at

a 220 px width, the filament menu in an old order), instead of from the two sources that are authoritative.

**Why:** rule 5 of "Writing UI code" (agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md) says the design system wins, and the
design system's truth is its coded bundle (`figma-mirror/published/ds/project/components/bundle.css`, classes
`.jp-*`), not any one board on the canvas: boards drift (the printer-menu board draws rows at 13 px, the reply
choice board draws the pre-capsule style). For surfaces the bundle has no component for (the printer receipt, a
sent photo in a message), the app's own CSS and TSX are the source.

**How to apply:** before drawing a board, dump the bundle rules for every component used (`grep '\.jp-<name>'
bundle.css`) and read the app's row set for every menu (Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp, Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp,
HomeUI PrinterMenu.tsx) and the app's CSS for chat pieces (AgentUI/styles.css). Also wrong the first time: the chat header named the project where the app names the chat (3 to 7 words, kConversationTitleInstructions); the pinned card was the stale "CURRENT SETUP · See all" board, not the app's Setup summary (`.current-setup*`: label + state header in Metadata Bold, purpose as Body Bold title, presets line, plan headline, Label Bold metrics with 14 px glyphs, hairline, All settings link; out of date drops the accent and uses the attention block); the composer placeholder was not the approved board's. Draw rows at Body 14 / 36 px
(`.jp-menu-row`), popovers on surface-raised 280 wide, reply choices as capsules on surface-subtle, user
bubbles 10/12 padding radius-medium at 75% width, tool cards on surface-subtle, project cards 293 wide with
one status line, and no annotation tags ("NEW") inside a drawn component. State in the caption which rows are
new. Known DS-vs-canvas inconsistency not mine to settle: `.jp-bubble-agent` has an avatar; the app and the
timeline boards draw agent prose without one. Related: [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]],
[[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[calibration-design-decisions]].

description: "The two Claude artifacts mirroring the Figma file JusPrin v2 (a Design System and a Design canvas): URLs, where the re-sync tools and backups live, how a re-sync is proven safe, what was measured on 2026-10-13, known gaps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 18e047ce-4892-4a44-8b70-c447eb34727c
  modified: 2026-10-13T20:50:06.847Z
---

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.

Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=<tmp>` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then.

**Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts`
were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added
directly in the artifact). Running build_components.py or assembling from those sources regresses the live
bundle. Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools

a 220 px width, the filament menu in an old order), instead of from the two sources that are authoritative.

design system's truth is its coded bundle (`figma-mirror/published/ds/project/components/bundle.css`, classes
`.jp-*`), not any one board on the canvas: boards drift (the printer-menu board draws rows at 13 px, the reply
choice board draws the pre-capsule style). For surfaces the bundle has no component for (the printer receipt, a
sent photo in a message), the app's own CSS and TSX are the source.

**How to apply:** before drawing a board, dump the bundle rules for every component used (`grep '\.jp-<name>'
bundle.css`) and read the app's row set for every menu (Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp, Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp,
HomeUI PrinterMenu.tsx) and the app's CSS for chat pieces (AgentUI/styles.css). Also wrong the first time: the chat header named the project where the app names the chat (3 to 7 words, kConversationTitleInstructions); the pinned card was the stale "CURRENT SETUP · See all" board, not the app's Setup summary (`.current-setup*`: label + state header in Metadata Bold, purpose as Body Bold title, presets line, plan headline, Label Bold metrics with 14 px glyphs, hairline, All settings link; out of date drops the accent and uses the attention block); the composer placeholder was not the approved board's. Draw rows at Body 14 / 36 px
(`.jp-menu-row`), popovers on surface-raised 280 wide, reply choices as capsules on surface-subtle, user
bubbles 10/12 padding radius-medium at 75% width, tool cards on surface-subtle, project cards 293 wide with
one status line, and no annotation tags ("NEW") inside a drawn component. State in the caption which rows are
new. Known DS-vs-canvas inconsistency not mine to settle: `.jp-bubble-agent` has an avatar; the app and the
timeline boards draw agent prose without one. Related: [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]],
[[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[calibration-design-decisions]].

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.

Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=<tmp>` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then.

**Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts`
were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added
directly in the artifact). Running build_components.py or assembling from those sources regresses the live
bundle. Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools

---
name: first-run-flow-sequence
description: "Kenneth's 2026-11-02 first-run flow after the welcome: a sequence Welcome → Printers → Home owned by a controller, with the agent doors as detours that return (sign-in waits on the card, Preferences closes back, Just slice skips the detour not the sequence); Printers step imports OrcaSlicer or adds/assumes a printer; what the canvas still lacks."
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided 2026-11-02, late, after Kenneth asked how Preferences gets back to the OrcaSlicer import and how "Just slice for now" returns to onboarding ("I don't think you have thought through").

- **Shape:** onboarding is a sequence, Welcome → Printers → Home. A controller owns the step. Preferences (a modal `PreferencesWindow`, returns on close) and the browser sign-in (loopback callback on port 41172, polled by `CloudSignIn::poll()`) are detours off step 1; when one finishes the controller advances. Nothing a detour does strands the person outside the sequence.
- **Welcome doors:** Sign in → browser; the card shows "Finish signing in in your browser" with Cancel, other doors dimmed; on the callback the card flips to "Signed in as … · 500 credits", then step 2. Own key / MCP → Preferences › Agent opens modal on that section; saving a verified key or Done closes it and advances; closing unfinished returns to the welcome with nothing chosen. Just slice → step 2 at once.
- **Printers step:** the app needs one printer (an empty data folder has none). OrcaSlicer folder found → "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?" with Import (copies user presets like `V1Import`, but asked, not silent) and Start fresh. JusPrin v1 found → step skipped, the existing welcome-back window shows over Home. Neither → the add-printer form with "Skip, use a default", which installs the default and marks the chip assumed. Back returns to the welcome; finished detours stay done. A 3MF opened on first launch still shows the welcome, then skips this step ("from the file").
- **Home:** first-run state reflects the choices: agent connected and the 500 credits shown once, or the three doors collapsed in the agent column after Just slice; the Printers column lists imported/added/assumed.
- **Quit mid-flow:** done is marked only when Home is reached; next launch shows the welcome again with finished detours reflected.

**Why:** the first design named destinations and skipped transitions; Kenneth wants every door to come back into one flow.

**How to apply:** build the controller first, then the screens. Drawn on the canvas in version 89 (2026-11-02) as first-run-04 to first-run-11 (11 is the flow board); the old wizard boards onboarding-00 to 20 sit at the bottom of the page under a superseded note. Choices the decision didn't cover (an Agent group in Home's right column, doors dimmed on the signed-in card) are listed in the repo-root note first-run-flow-design-2026-11.md. Related: [[first-run-value-prop-decisions]], [[first-run-flow-boards]], [[agent-setup-one-flow-decisions]].

**Built 2026-11-03** on `claude/first-run-flow-f7be35` (four commits ending 914e48b77f, off `credits-integration-2026-11`, not pushed, no PR; worktree `.claude/worktrees/first-run-flow-f7be35`, owned by session local_cea7b182). Tests and the shell harness (`--fresh-example`, 40 checks) pass. Checked in the built app: welcome, sign-in door, add-printer form. Not run there: own-key, MCP, Just slice, Import, Skip, Home. Steps left: `first-run-flow-live-checks-left.md` at the repo root (untracked). Not built: a 3MF opened on first launch skipping Printers. The clip is the placeholder animatic at `resources/jusprin/welcome/welcome-clip.mp4`; CC BY credits sit in a "Photo credits" disclosure under the clip, not the About box. Never press "Sign in for 500 credits" on Kenneth's Mac during a check: the browser is signed in and it completes by itself.

**2026-11-03 afternoon:** the sign-in door is now Google + email (code or password), with an import result screen and the v1 line; see [[old-onboarding-boards-review]] for commits, tests and gaps. App branch `claude/first-run-flow-f7be35` (3df2ed9c24), gateway branch `claude/email-sign-in` in tsd-enterprise (81efc6fd43). Not pushed.
---
name: old-onboarding-boards-review
description: "2026-11-03 review of the original (frozen-canvas) onboarding boards against the built first-run flow; what the old flow had that the new one dropped, and which pieces were judged worth taking back."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e997298c-6edf-4c7d-8994-08bc7e301a34
  modified: 2026-11-03T13:54:12.107Z
---

Kenneth asked (2026-11-03) whether the new first-run flow dropped the email-code sign-up on purpose. It did not: the welcome was designed from the credits branch's sign-in code without reading the old boards. He then asked for a look at the old flow for anything worth keeping.

**Where the old flow is:** the frozen canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v), boards `project/onboarding-00` … `-20`, `onboarding-v1-01..03`, the `onboarding-delivery-*` notes, and the design-system component `ds-field-verification-code`. Text of 26 of them extracted to the session scratchpad `old-onboarding/`.

**What the old flow had that the built flow (claude/first-run-flow-f7be35) lacks:**
- Sign-in: Google in the browser plus an email code typed in the app (six cells, auto-verify on the sixth digit, expired-code state, Resend / Change email / Use Google instead); a "couldn't return automatically" recovery with a Check sign-in button; a Terms and Privacy line. New flow: browser only, a waiting state with Cancel and one error line. No code endpoint exists on the server; the live Obico sign-up is email + password.
- After sign-in: "checking AI access" and "AI unavailable: Try again / Continue locally". New flow goes straight to Printers; the account card showed no balance when the gateway 404'd.
- OrcaSlicer import: choose the folder manually or a preset bundle when nothing is detected; a partial-result screen (conflicts renamed "(Orca copy)", failures with reasons, Retry failed items). New flow: one list, Import / Start fresh / Back; conflicts go through a yes/no dialog mid-import.
- First project: "Try the example" (3DBenchy) beside Open. New Home empty state has only New / Open; the example was removed with the Project step.
- v1 users: a Welcome back card listing what was copied, "the same account you used in v1", and a sign-in-expired variant. New flow keeps WelcomeBackWindow separately but the welcome's sign-in door still says "Your first month: 500 credits" to everyone.
- Project load failed: "No existing work was replaced", native reason, Retry / Choose another. General file-open behaviour, not onboarding.

**My ranking (Kenneth has not ruled yet):** take the example model on Home's empty state and a v1-aware sign-in door first; then the browser-return recovery and the Terms line; then the import result report. The email code is a server project and a second sign-in path; recommend deferring it.

**How to apply:** when Kenneth rules, record the decision here and in [[first-run-flow-sequence]]; the boards named above are the reference for wording and states. Related: [[first-run-value-prop-decisions]], [[v1-subscribers-grandfathered]].

**Kenneth's rulings, 2026-11-03 morning:** no example model ("No need for example models"); the email code goes in ("taking the users of the app into browser is not the best user experience. Email code keeps the user in the app"); everything else I listed he agreed with (v1-aware door, browser-return recovery, Terms line, import result, "checking AI" belongs on Home's agent card). He also asked for proof that the pricing work on `credits-integration-2026-11` is fully carried into the flow.

**Pricing audit result:** the first-run branch touched only the onboarding screens, Home's agent group (reusing `balanceRows`) and Preferences' close-when-done; pickers, ring and panel, pre-send check, 402 card, low-balance notice, print-report form, the welcome-back window (boards 1c/1d) and the Preferences account row (1a) are untouched from the credits branch. One drift: the scale line under the offer reads "Then paid, or your own key." and must be the decided "An Expert message is 5 credits. Your own API key stays free." Step 3 (Chargebee, Account and pricing pages, v1 carry-over) is unbuilt on both branches, and production's gateway lacks the ledger branch, which is why the account card showed no balance.

**Email-code design (renders `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/12a..12d`, generator `value-prop-2026-11/tagline/build8.py`):** the offer card keeps the decided headline, scale line and "Sign in for 500 credits" button, with an email field beside the button; under it "We email you a 6-digit code. No password." and a link to the browser (Google or a password); a Terms and Privacy line. Pressing the button swaps the card for "Check your email." with six cells that sign in on the sixth digit, Resend / Change email / Use the browser instead / Cancel; an expired or wrong code turns the cells red with "Send a new code". The browser state gains "Nothing happened? Open the browser again · Check sign-in" and "Use an email code instead". Placeholder address is always alex@example.com.

**Server facts for the code:** the gateway authenticates OAuth2 bearer tokens of any application (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/auth.py`); the app's OAuth app is "JusPrin2" (public, PKCE). The Obico server runs django-allauth 0.63.6, whose login-by-code only serves existing users and has no API in that version, so the code sign-in is two new gateway endpoints (request a code; confirm it and issue a JusPrin2 access token), creating the user when the email is unknown the way the adapter does (username `email_syndicateid`). Trap: `ACCOUNT_UNIQUE_EMAIL = False`, so one email can own several accounts; the confirm step must pick deterministically (most recently active in the JusPrin syndicate) and say so in a comment.

**2026-11-03, Kenneth: "Change first", then "Any reason why we shouldn't offer multiple ways for users to sign in? … I don't think we should be creative here because this is literally the first entry area."** Checked online and against the nine captured sign-in screens (`value-prop-2026-11/logo-refs/`): every one offers Google; most are identifier-first (one email field, no sign-in/sign-up split: Notion, Dropbox, Spotify, Zoom, Linear); Notion, Slack and Linear then send a code, Figma, GitHub and Stripe ask a password; 2–3 visible options is the norm. Hard constraint: Google has blocked OAuth inside embedded webviews since 2017 and RFC 8252 says native apps use the system browser, so "Continue with Google" is a browser round trip in any desktop app; email code and password can stay in the app. Re-rendered as `first-run-2026-11/13a` (offer card: Continue with Google, "or", email field + Continue with email, Terms line) and `13b` (identifier-first password step for an address that has one, with "Email me a code instead"); generator `tagline/build9.py`. Trade-off noted: with two buttons the button no longer names the reward; the offer stays the card's headline. Not yet ruled.

**Ruled and built, 2026-11-03 afternoon.** Kenneth: "Yes, build it" on the conventional door (Google first, one email field, then a 6-digit code in the app or a password for an address that has one), and "Tail that subsession to build this": the existing implementation session did both halves. App: five commits on `claude/first-run-flow-f7be35` ending 3df2ed9c24 (door states, `CodeField.tsx`, import result screen with "Retry failed items" and the folder-picker link, v1 line, scale-line fix, harness email checks; 3df2ed9c24 fixes Home's poll, which only reported a phase change and left the page on "busy" between email steps). Gateway: 81efc6fd43 on `claude/email-sign-in` in tsd-enterprise (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/sign_in.py`, four endpoints under `auth/`, codes as HMAC in Redis, tokens minted for client id "JusPrin2", templates under `web_ent/jusprin/templates/jusprin/v2/email/`). One deviation from the brief, kept: an account made through Google gets a code, not the password step, because its password is random. Tests: 155 gateway tests passed (23 new), 515 + 160 Catch2 cases, 141 Vitest; a mutation run with the ordering and social-account logic removed failed 4 tests, so they bite. Built app against the local compose stack: code path (wrong, expired, resent, right) and password path (wrong, right) both saved the account. Pictures of nine door states, light and dark, in `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/built/door/`; they are page replays of real app states, not window captures; the browser-wait and v1-line pictures are hand-delivered states. Not verified: Windows, Linux, Continue with Google, the import result screen in the real app, a real v1 import. Known gaps: renamed imported printers leave their filaments' `compatible_printers` on the old name; no hidden username field for password managers; the welcome's clip card stays white in dark mode. Nothing pushed, no PR.

**Later the same day, driven by Kenneth in the implementation session:** aa70569e4f rebuilt `sign_in.py` on what the website already runs (SyndicateSpecificBackend lookup, allauth adapter sign-up and `authenticate()`, allauth's rate limiter for codes, django-oauth-toolkit's own token server); only the Redis code store stays custom, because allauth 0.63's login-by-code looks across syndicates and makes no account. d799b57e37 dropped the duplicate-address test: production's 251,485 accounts have no two in one syndicate sharing an address, so the lookup raises like the website instead of picking one. Kenneth then asked (through the session "btw: Why not?") for a task card to upgrade django-allauth to 65.x on the same branch and worktree first, with the rebuild on allauth's flows after; the card could not carry the folder, so it was offered as a question instead.

**2026-11-03, Kenneth: "Change first", then "Any reason why we shouldn't offer multiple ways for users to sign in? … I don't think we should be creative here because this is literally the first entry area."** Checked online and against the nine captured sign-in screens (`value-prop-2026-11/logo-refs/`): every one offers Google; most are identifier-first (one email field, no sign-in/sign-up split: Notion, Dropbox, Spotify, Zoom, Linear); Notion, Slack and Linear then send a code, Figma, GitHub and Stripe ask a password; 2–3 visible options is the norm. Hard constraint: Google has blocked OAuth inside embedded webviews since 2017 and RFC 8252 says native apps use the system browser, so "Continue with Google" is a browser round trip in any desktop app; email code and password can stay in the app. Re-rendered as `first-run-2026-11/13a` (offer card: Continue with Google, "or", email field + Continue with email, Terms line) and `13b` (identifier-first password step for an address that has one, with "Email me a code instead"); generator `tagline/build9.py`. Trade-off noted: with two buttons the button no longer names the reward; the offer stays the card's headline. Not yet ruled.

**Ruled and built, 2026-11-03 afternoon.** Kenneth: "Yes, build it" on the conventional door (Google first, one email field, then a 6-digit code in the app or a password for an address that has one), and "Tail that subsession to build this": the existing implementation session did both halves. App: five commits on `claude/first-run-flow-f7be35` ending 3df2ed9c24 (door states, `CodeField.tsx`, import result screen with "Retry failed items" and the folder-picker link, v1 line, scale-line fix, harness email checks; 3df2ed9c24 fixes Home's poll, which only reported a phase change and left the page on "busy" between email steps). Gateway: 81efc6fd43 on `claude/email-sign-in` in tsd-enterprise (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/sign_in.py`, four endpoints under `auth/`, codes as HMAC in Redis, tokens minted for client id "JusPrin2", templates under `web_ent/jusprin/templates/jusprin/v2/email/`). One deviation from the brief, kept: an account made through Google gets a code, not the password step, because its password is random. Tests: 155 gateway tests passed (23 new), 515 + 160 Catch2 cases, 141 Vitest; a mutation run with the ordering and social-account logic removed failed 4 tests, so they bite. Built app against the local compose stack: code path (wrong, expired, resent, right) and password path (wrong, right) both saved the account. Pictures of nine door states, light and dark, in `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/built/door/`; they are page replays of real app states, not window captures; the browser-wait and v1-line pictures are hand-delivered states. Not verified: Windows, Linux, Continue with Google, the import result screen in the real app, a real v1 import. Known gaps: renamed imported printers leave their filaments' `compatible_printers` on the old name; no hidden username field for password managers; the welcome's clip card stays white in dark mode. Nothing pushed, no PR.

**Later the same day, driven by Kenneth in the implementation session:** aa70569e4f rebuilt `sign_in.py` on what the website already runs (SyndicateSpecificBackend lookup, allauth adapter sign-up and `authenticate()`, allauth's rate limiter for codes, django-oauth-toolkit's own token server); only the Redis code store stays custom, because allauth 0.63's login-by-code looks across syndicates and makes no account. d799b57e37 dropped the duplicate-address test: production's 251,485 accounts have no two in one syndicate sharing an address, so the lookup raises like the website instead of picking one. Kenneth then asked (through the session "btw: Why not?") for a task card to upgrade django-allauth to 65.x on the same branch and worktree first, with the rebuild on allauth's flows after; the card could not carry the folder, so it was offered as a question instead.

#!/bin/zsh
# e2e.sh <light|dark> <code|password>
# The built app on an empty data folder, signed in by email against the local
# gateway (localhost:3534), with a screenshot of the window at each door state.
D=${0:A:h}; cd $D
APP=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/first-run-flow-f7be35/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
theme=$1; flow=$2
SHOTS=$D/../shots/door; mkdir -p $SHOTS
R=$D/e2e-$theme-$flow; rm -rf $R; mkdir -p $R/JusPrin
print '{"jusprin_server": {"base_url": "http://localhost:3534"}}' > $R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf
: > drive.log
# The local stack's hourly limits, which repeated runs would reach.
docker exec email-sign-in-redis-1 sh -c "redis-cli --scan --pattern '*allauth:rl:*' | xargs -r redis-cli DEL" > /dev/null
ARGS=(--datadir $R/JusPrin); [[ $theme == dark ]] && ARGS+=(-AppleInterfaceStyle Dark)
JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/home.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/agent.html \
  $APP $ARGS > $D/e2e-$theme-$flow.out 2>&1 &
P=$!
trap 'kill $P 2>/dev/null' EXIT

js(){ ./drive.sh home "$1" | sed 's/^home  RESULT //'; }
# until <name> <js condition>: polls the page for up to 30 s.
until_true(){ for i in {1..60}; do [[ $(js "String(Boolean($2))") == true ]] && { echo "ok $1"; return 0; }; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "TIMEOUT $1: $(js 'JSON.stringify({signIn: __last?.onboarding.signIn, email: __last?.onboarding.email, err: __last?.onboarding.signInError})')"; return 1; }
# This shell may not capture the screen, so each door state is saved as the
# state the app sent the page, for replaying into the same page bundle.
STATES=$D/../states; mkdir -p $STATES
shot(){ sleep 0.8; CUT=400000 ./drive.sh home "JSON.stringify(__last)" | sed 's/^home  RESULT //' > $STATES/$1.json && echo "state $1 ($(wc -c < $STATES/$1.json) bytes)"; }
EMAIL=__last?.onboarding.email

for i in {1..120}; do grep -q "^home state" drive.log && break; sleep 0.5; done
until_true welcome "__last?.onboarding.step === 'welcome'" || exit 1
js "window.resizeTo && 'ready'" > /dev/null
shot 13a-rest

if [[ $flow == code ]]; then
  # States the real app cannot reach here: the browser wait needs Continue
  # with Google, which this Mac must not press, and the v1 line a v1 import.
  js "fake({signIn: 'browser'})"; shot 12d-browser-wait-delivered
  js "fake({signIn: 'idle', v1Imported: true})"; shot 13a-v1-line-delivered
  js "fake({v1Imported: false})" > /dev/null

  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', 'alex@example.com')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
  until_true code-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'code' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot 12b-code
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '000000')"
  until_true wrong-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_code'" || exit 1
  shot 12c-wrong-code
  # The ten-minute expiry, as Redis does it.
  docker exec email-sign-in-redis-1 sh -c "redis-cli --scan --pattern '*sign_in:code:alex@example.com' | xargs -r redis-cli DEL" > /dev/null
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '111111')"
  until_true expired-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'expired_code'" || exit 1
  shot 12c-expired-code
  js "clickText('Send a new code')"
  until_true code-resent "$EMAIL?.codeResent === true && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  sleep 1; CODE=$(../latest_code.sh 1m); echo "emailed code read from the local mail backend (${#CODE} digits)"
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '$CODE')"
else
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', 'alex@example.com')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
  until_true password-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'password' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot 13b-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', 'not the password')"; js "clickText('Sign in')"
  until_true wrong-password "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_password'" || exit 1
  shot 13b-wrong-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', '$(cat ../test-password)')" > /dev/null; js "clickText('Sign in')"
fi
until_true signed-in "__last?.onboarding.accountEmail === 'alex@example.com'" || exit 1
shot signed-in-$flow
js "JSON.stringify({signIn: __last.onboarding.signIn, err: __last.onboarding.signInError, step: __last.onboarding.step})"
python3 -c "import json; c=json.load(open('$R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf')); a=c.get('jusprin_agent', {}); print('saved', sorted(k for k in a if 'jusprin' in k))"

queues = collections.defaultdict(list)

<script>
(function(){
  const tag = location.pathname.includes('agent') ? 'agent' : 'home';
  const base = 'http://127.0.0.1:8766';
  const post = (q, body) => fetch(base + '/log?page=' + tag + q, {method: 'POST', body});
  async function tick() {
    try {
      const t = await (await fetch(base + '/cmd?page=' + tag)).text();
      if (t) { let out; try { out = await eval(t); } catch (e) { out = 'ERR ' + e; } await post('', 'RESULT ' + String(out)); }
    } catch (e) {}
    setTimeout(tick, 300);
  }
  tick();
  const wrap = setInterval(() => {
    if (window.__jusprinBridge && window.wx) {
      clearInterval(wrap);
      const d = window.__jusprinBridge.deliver.bind(window.__jusprinBridge);
      window.__jusprinBridge.deliver = (e) => { if (e.type === 'state') window.__last = e.payload; post('&env=' + e.type, 'IN ' + JSON.stringify(e.payload).slice(0, 3000)); return d(e); };
      const p = window.wx.postMessage.bind(window.wx);
      window.wx.postMessage = (j) => { try { const m = JSON.parse(j); post('&env=' + m.type, 'OUT ' + JSON.stringify(m.payload).slice(0, 500)); } catch (e) {} return p(j); };
    }
  }, 20);
  window.clickText = (t) => {
    const all = [...document.querySelectorAll('button,summary')];
    const b = all.find(x => x.textContent.trim() === t || x.getAttribute('aria-label') === t) || all.find(x => x.textContent.trim().startsWith(t));
    if (!b) return 'no button ' + t + ' among ' + all.map(x => x.textContent.trim()).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 30).join(' | ');
    b.click(); return 'clicked ' + t + (b.disabled ? ' (disabled)' : '');
  };
  window.typeInto = (sel, v) => {
    const el = document.querySelector(sel);
    if (!el) return 'no ' + sel;
    Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set.call(el, v);
    el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}));
    return 'typed ' + sel;
  };
  // Re-delivers the host's last state with the onboarding patched, for states
  // the real host cannot reach here.
  window.fake = (patch) => {
    const s = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(window.__last));
    Object.assign(s.onboarding, patch);
    window.__jusprinBridge.deliver({protocol: 'jusprin-home-bridge', version: 1, id: 'fake-' + Date.now(), type: 'state', payload: s});
    return 'faked ' + JSON.stringify(patch);
  };
  window.text = () => document.body.innerText.slice(0, 1500);
})();
</script>

#!/bin/zsh
# e2e.sh <code|password>: the built app on an empty data folder, signed in by
# email against the one-off server on localhost:3536, through the welcome's
# email door. Each door state the app sends the page is saved for pictures.
D=${0:A:h}; cd $D
APP=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/first-run-flow-f7be35/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
flow=$1
R=$D/e2e-$flow; rm -rf $R; mkdir -p $R/JusPrin
print '{"jusprin_server": {"base_url": "http://localhost:3536"}}' > $R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf
: > drive.log
JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/home.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/home.html \
  $APP --datadir $R/JusPrin > $D/e2e-$flow.out 2>&1 &
P=$!
trap 'kill $P 2>/dev/null' EXIT
js(){ ./drive.sh home "$1" | sed 's/^home  RESULT //'; }
until_true(){ for i in {1..60}; do [[ $(js "String(Boolean($2))") == true ]] && { echo "ok $1"; return 0; }; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "TIMEOUT $1: $(js 'JSON.stringify({signIn: __last?.onboarding.signIn, email: __last?.onboarding.email, err: __last?.onboarding.signInError})')"; return 1; }
STATES=$D/../states; mkdir -p $STATES
shot(){ sleep 0.8; CUT=400000 ./drive.sh home "JSON.stringify(__last)" | sed 's/^home  RESULT //' > $STATES/$1.json && echo "state $1"; }
auth_requests(){ docker logs email-e2e-web 2>&1 | grep -c '"POST /ent/jusprin/v2/auth/'; }
latest_code(){ docker logs --since 2m email-e2e-web 2>&1 | grep -A2 "sign-in code is" | grep -Eo '^[0-9]{6}$' | tail -1; }
EMAIL=__last?.onboarding.email

for i in {1..120}; do grep -q "^home state" drive.log && break; sleep 0.5; done
until_true welcome "__last?.onboarding.step === 'welcome'" || exit 1
before=$(auth_requests)
if [[ $flow == code ]]; then ADDRESS=new-$(date +%s)@example.com; else ADDRESS=pw@example.com; fi
js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', '$ADDRESS')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
until_true choice "$EMAIL?.step === 'choose' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
sleep 1; echo "auth requests after Continue with email: $(( $(auth_requests) - before ))"
shot choose-$flow

if [[ $flow == code ]]; then
  js "clickText('Email me a 6-digit code')"
  until_true code-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'code' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot code
  CODE=$(latest_code); echo "emailed code read from the server's console mail (${#CODE} digits)"
  WRONG=$(printf '%06d' $(( (10#$CODE + 1) % 1000000 )))
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '$WRONG')"
  until_true wrong-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_code' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot code-wrong
  for n in 2 3 4 5; do js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '$WRONG')" > /dev/null
    until_true wrong-$n "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_code' && !$EMAIL?.busy" > /dev/null || exit 1; done
  # Five wrong tries spend the code: even the right one no longer works.
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '$CODE')"
  until_true spent-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'expired_code' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot code-spent
  js "clickText('Send a new code')"
  until_true code-resent "$EMAIL?.codeResent === true && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot code-resent
  sleep 1; CODE=$(latest_code); echo "new code read (${#CODE} digits)"
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '$CODE')"
else
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', 'not the password')"; js "clickText('Sign in')"
  until_true wrong-password "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_password' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot choose-wrong-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', '$(cat ../test-password)')" > /dev/null; js "clickText('Sign in')"
fi
until_true signed-in "__last?.onboarding.accountEmail === '$ADDRESS'" || exit 1
shot signed-in-$flow
js "JSON.stringify({signIn: __last.onboarding.signIn, err: __last.onboarding.signInError, step: __last.onboarding.step})"
python3 -c "import json; c=json.load(open('$R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf')); print('conf keys with jusprin account', sorted(k for k,v in c.items() if 'cloud' in k or 'account' in k))"
EOF
chmod +x $S/drive/e2e.sh; cd $S/drive && (python3 server.py 8766 > server.out 2>&1 &) ; sleep 1; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8766/home.html; grep -n "jusprin_server\|base_url" /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/first-run-flow-f7be35/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp | head -3

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Throws and log lines may name Orca; they never reach the model.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Throws and log lines may name Orca; they never reach the model.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. ## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.

- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
